project.name: OR Intelligence
project.tagline: Laparoscopic instrument detection → clickable instrument timeline for surgical education
project.description: A web-based surgical video review platform. A reviewer uploads a recorded laparoscopic cholecystectomy; a fine-tuned YOLO detector locates 6 instruments (grasper, bipolar, hook, scissors, clipper, irrigator) in sampled frames; temporal smoothing removes flicker; the result is a colour-coded instrument timeline where clicking a bar jumps the video to that moment. Sessions export as a PDF report with timestamped instructor notes (English / Arabic).
objectives: Detect the 6 main laparoscopic instruments per frame with a fine-tuned YOLO model.
Convert per-frame detections into a smoothed instrument-usage timeline (intervals + per-case statistics).
Deliver a web app: upload → timeline → jump-to-moment → timestamped notes → PDF report.
Support the 5 use cases: self-review, instructor feedback, searchable library, case-conference clip finding, training analytics.
Measure success with mAP@0.5 + per-class P/R, timeline agreement with ground-truth presence labels, and a time-to-find usability test.

deliverables.name: Labelled YOLO dataset + video-level split + EDA report
Trained YOLO weights + evaluation report (mAP@0.5, per-class P/R) + model card
Timeline engine (smoothing, intervals, statistics) + timeline evaluation
Web app: review workspace, notes, library search, analytics, Arabic/RTL
Usability study results (manual scrubbing vs timeline)
Final report, README, slide deck, demo video

requirements.text: Detect 6 instruments per frame (grasper, bipolar, hook, scissors, clipper, irrigator)
Model metrics: mAP@0.5 and per-instrument precision/recall on a video-level held-out test set
Temporal smoothing to remove flicker
Colour-coded instrument timeline (e.g. hook 03:10–09:45)
Timeline agreement with ground-truth presence labels
Upload a recorded video and process it
Click a timeline bar to jump the video to that moment
Timestamped instructor notes
PDF report export including instructor notes
Searchable library indexed by instrument ("show all clipping segments")
Find unusual tool patterns / clips quickly (long irrigation, repeated switches)
Per-case statistics: time per instrument, total time, tool switches; compare across cases
Arabic-language interface and reports
requirements.source: Gap in existing tools / business model

requirements.text: Usability test: time to find a moment, scrubbing vs timeline
Public research data only; non-commercial licence; educational, not diagnostic
Problem definition, use cases and business model documented
Final project report and presentation

assumptions: Team of 4 (Members A–D). Real names are not yet known: they are editable in the dashboard and stored locally.
No code exists yet; every task except 1.1.1 (problem & use-case page, which exists) starts as Not Started.

Hard deadline: Wednesday 25 Nov 2026, 23:59. Work starts Monday 23 Nov evening, which gives 7 working blocks of about 4–5 h. Each member's load is about 25 h, so this is an MVP plan: one baseline model plus 1–2 tuning runs, a small usability test, and a one-command local run instead of a hardened deployment.

Bounding-box training data comes from m2cai16-tool-locations (public, VOC-format boxes). Timeline ground truth uses Cholec80 tool-presence labels (1 fps) if the team already has access. A new Cholec80 access request will likely not be approved before Wednesday, so the fallback is presence labels from the m2cai16-tool videos that are held out from detection training (task 1.3.1 decides on Monday evening).

Stack: Python 3.11, Ultralytics YOLO (v8/11), FastAPI + SQLite, React + Vite + TypeScript, ReportLab for PDF. A free GPU (Kaggle or Colab) is used for training; training runs in the background while members build other modules.
Daily sync: 10-minute stand-up at 09:00 Tue and Wed, plus a 21:00 merge window each evening run by Member D.

Owns everything between detections and the browser: temporal smoothing, interval building and statistics, timeline evaluation, the FastAPI service, notes/search/analytics endpoints and the PDF report.

Team lead and integration owner. Owns the repo scaffold, interface contracts and fixtures, the web review workspace and library, the one-command local run, smoke tests, merging to develop/main and final report assembly.

tasks.name: Dataset licensing & ethics checklist
tasks.desc: Confirm which datasets may be used, under what licence, how to cite them, and record the educational/non-diagnostic scope. Blocks any data download.
steps: Read the licence and access terms of m2cai16-tool-locations, m2cai16-tool and Cholec80 (CAMMA research licences, non-commercial).

Decide tonight (Mon) on the timeline ground truth: Cholec80 only if a team member already has access; otherwise m2cai16-tool presence labels on held-out videos. Record the decision in the doc and tell C.
List allowed uses (academic project, no redistribution of raw videos in the repo, no commercial use).
Write the BibTeX citations required by each dataset.
Write docs/data/LICENSES_AND_ETHICS.md: licences, citations, storage rule (data/ is gitignored), 'educational tool, not diagnostic' statement, PDPL note for any future real-patient data.
accept: Document lists licence, citation and allowed use for every dataset used.
Reviewed and approved by D in PR.
Explicit rule: no raw video or frames committed to Git.

tasks.name: Download & verify datasets
tasks.desc: Scripted, reproducible download of m2cai16-tool-locations (frames + VOC XML boxes) and the Cholec80 videos/tool annotations needed for timeline evaluation, with checksums.
steps: Write src/data/download.py: CLI `python -m src.data.download --dataset m2cai16|cholec80 --out data/raw/` (Cholec80 path may be a manual copy if the licence requires manual download; script then only verifies).
Record SHA-256 of every archive in configs/data.yaml under `checksums:`.
Write src/data/verify.py: counts images, XML files, videos and tool-annotation files; fails loudly on mismatch.
Store raw data in data/raw/m2cai16_tool_locations/ and data/raw/cholec80/ (gitignored).
Put a 20-frame sample + 1 XML in tests/unit/data/sample/ for unit tests (only if the licence allows; otherwise synthetic boxes).
Upload a team copy to the shared drive so B and C don't re-download.
accept: `python -m src.data.verify` passes on a clean machine after download.
Counts printed match the dataset documentation.
Nothing under data/ is tracked by Git.

tasks.name: VOC → YOLO conversion & class mapping
tasks.desc: Convert m2cai16-tool-locations Pascal-VOC boxes into YOLO txt labels using contracts/classes.json, dropping SpecimenBag, with validation and visual spot-checks.
steps: Write src/data/convert_voc_to_yolo.py: parse XML, map names case-insensitively (Grasper→0 … Irrigator→5), skip SpecimenBag, clip boxes to image bounds, write `cls cx cy w h` normalised.
Log and count: dropped boxes, empty images, malformed XML. Keep images with zero tools as background images (empty .txt).
Write src/data/visualize.py: draws labels on N random images to data/processed/qa/.
Manually inspect ≥50 rendered images; note issues in docs/data/qa_notes.md.
Unit tests tests/unit/data/test_convert.py: known XML → expected txt; out-of-bounds box clipped; SpecimenBag dropped.
accept: Every image has exactly one .txt label file (possibly empty).
All class ids ∈ {0..5}; all coordinates ∈ [0,1].
≥50 visual spot-checks recorded with <2% label errors.
Unit tests pass in CI.

tasks.name: Video-level train/val/test split
tasks.desc: Split by source video (never by frame) so the test set measures generalisation to unseen surgeries, as required by the success measures.
steps: Parse the video ID from each frame filename; build a video → frame count table.
Write src/data/split.py: deterministic (seed 42) split ≈70/15/15 by video, stratified so each split contains all 6 classes.
Write data/splits/splits.json and place images/labels into train/val/test folders.
Generate data/processed/dataset.yaml (Ultralytics format; names from contracts/classes.json).
Add a leakage test: assert no video ID appears in more than one split.
Hand off: post split counts (videos, images, boxes per class per split) in the PR and tag B.
accept: No video ID shared across splits (test passes).
Each split contains every class at least 20 times.
`yolo detect val data=data/processed/dataset.yaml` loads the dataset without errors.

tasks.name: Timeline ground truth from Cholec80 presence labels
tasks.desc: Prepare a held-out set of full surgery videos with per-second tool-presence labels, used to measure timeline agreement (success measure 2). Videos must not overlap with the detector's training videos. Source is Cholec80 or the m2cai16-tool fallback (decided in 1.3.1).

Check and document that none of these videos are the source of any m2cai16 training frame (compare video identifiers/metadata; if uncertain, record as a risk).
Write src/data/presence_labels.py: convert the chosen tool-presence annotation files to contract C3 CSV (1 fps, map names to the 6 classes, drop SpecimenBag).
Write src/data/extract_frames.py (ffmpeg via subprocess): optional 1 fps frame dump for debugging.
Validate: CSV row count ≈ video duration in seconds (±2 s).
Hand off the CSVs and the video list to C (task 4.1.3).
accept: Each CSV matches contract C3 (header + 0/1 values).
Row counts within ±2 s of video length.
Overlap check with training videos documented.

tasks.name: EDA & class-balance report

steps: Write src/data/eda.py producing CSV + PNG charts in docs/data/figures/: boxes per class per split, images per video, box size distribution, co-occurrence matrix.
Summarise findings in notebooks/eda.ipynb (read-only visual companion).
Write docs/data/EDA.md: key numbers, imbalance ratio, small-object share, recommendations to B (e.g. oversample scissors/clipper).
accept: EDA.md contains per-class counts per split and at least 4 figures.
Recommendations section addressed to B is present.

tasks.name: Baseline YOLO training
tasks.desc: Fine-tune a COCO-pretrained YOLO (e.g. yolov8s / yolo11s) on the 6-class dataset to establish a baseline and produce first usable weights.
steps: Write configs/train.yaml (yolov8s, imgsz 640, epochs 50, batch 16, patience 10, seed 42, data path). Start the Kaggle/Colab run as early as possible Tue morning; it runs while you work on 3.3.1.
Write src/models/train.py wrapping Ultralytics: `python -m src.models.train --config configs/train.yaml --name baseline`.
Train on Colab/Kaggle GPU; log runs to runs/ and record experiment in docs/model/experiments.md (config hash, mAP@0.5, mAP@0.5:0.95, time).
Save best weights to models/weights/baseline.pt (store in shared drive / GitHub Release, never in Git).
Smoke test tests/unit/models/test_train_config.py (config loads, class names match contracts/classes.json).
accept: Baseline val mAP@0.5 recorded in experiments.md.
Weights downloadable by the team.
Training reproducible from the config with the same seed.

tasks.name: Augmentation & hyper-parameter experiments
tasks.desc: Improve on the baseline using EDA findings: model size, image size, augmentation (smoke/blur, HSV, mosaic), class imbalance handling. Select the final model on the validation split only.
steps: Plan 2 experiments in docs/model/experiments.md (one change each, chosen from EDA): e.g. imgsz 832 and blur/HSV augmentation or oversampling the rarest class. Launch both in parallel GPU sessions Tue afternoon.
Write src/models/tune.py to launch a named experiment from a config override file in configs/experiments/.
Run experiments; record val mAP@0.5 and per-class AP for each.
Choose the best by val mAP@0.5 (tie-break: per-class min AP, then speed). Do NOT look at the test split.
Export final weights models/weights/best.pt and optionally ONNX models/weights/best.onnx.
accept: 2 experiments logged with config and results (plus baseline).
Final model's val mAP@0.5 ≥ baseline.
best.pt shared by Tue 23:00; selection rationale written; test split untouched.

tasks.name: Held-out test evaluation report
tasks.desc: One-time evaluation of the final model on the video-level test split: mAP@0.5, mAP@0.5:0.95, per-instrument precision/recall, confusion matrix, failure analysis.
steps: Write src/models/evaluate.py: runs Ultralytics val on split=test, saves metrics JSON to docs/model/test_metrics.json.
Produce per-class P/R table at the chosen confidence threshold and PR curves.
Collect 20 failure cases (FN/FP) into docs/model/figures/failures/ with short comments (smoke, occlusion, motion blur, partial tools).
Write docs/model/EVALUATION.md.
Hand off the recommended confidence threshold to C (timeline params).
accept: Report includes mAP@0.5 and P/R for all 6 instruments on the test split.
Test split evaluated exactly once (stated in report).
Recommended conf threshold communicated to C in the PR.

tasks.name: Video inference module (detections.jsonl)
tasks.desc: Library + CLI that samples a video at N fps, runs the detector and streams detections in contract C4 format. This is what the API (C) calls.

CLI: `python -m src.inference.detect_video in.mp4 out.jsonl --fps 5`.
Fall back to CPU if no GPU; allow ONNX weights.
Tests tests/unit/inference/: run on tests/fixtures/sample_video.mp4 with baseline weights; output validates against contracts/detections.schema.json.

Progress callback reaches 1.0.

tasks.name: Model card & weights release
tasks.desc: Publish final weights as a GitHub Release asset with a model card describing data, metrics, limits and intended (educational) use.
steps: Write docs/model/MODEL_CARD.md: training data + licence, metrics table, known failure modes, intended use, out-of-scope (diagnosis, other procedures).
Create GitHub Release `model-v1` with best.pt (and best.onnx) and SHA-256.

tasks.name: Temporal smoothing
tasks.desc: Turn noisy per-frame detections into stable per-tool presence signals: confidence threshold, per-tool max-confidence per frame, sliding-window vote / hysteresis.
steps: Implement src/timeline/smoothing.py: `presence_matrix(dets, conf) -> np.ndarray[T, 6]` then `smooth(matrix, fps, window_s, method='majority'|'hysteresis', on=0.6, off=0.4)`.
Expose parameters in configs/timeline.yaml (conf, window_s, method, on/off thresholds).
Develop and test only against tests/fixtures/sample_detections.jsonl (no dependency on the real model).
Unit tests: single-frame flicker removed; real 3-s gap kept; output shape and dtype correct.
accept: Unit tests pass.
On the fixture, number of segments drops by ≥50% versus raw thresholding with no segment >2 s lost.

tasks.name: Interval builder & per-case statistics
tasks.desc: Convert smoothed presence into contract C5 timeline: intervals per tool (merge small gaps, drop tiny segments), per-tool time, segment counts, tool switches.
steps: Implement src/timeline/builder.py: `build_timeline(dets_path, video_id, params) -> dict` (contract C5).
Merge gaps < merge_gap_s; drop segments < min_segment_s; compute mean_conf per segment.
Define 'tool switch' = change in the set of active tools after smoothing; document the definition in the module docstring.
Compute stats: total_s, per_tool_s, per_tool_segments, switches.
Validate output against contracts/timeline.schema.json in tests.
CLI: `python -m src.timeline.builder detections.jsonl timeline.json`.
accept: Output validates against schema.
Hand-computed stats for the fixture match the module output.
Switch definition documented.

tasks.name: Timeline evaluation vs ground truth
tasks.desc: Measure success measure 2: agreement between predicted tool intervals and Cholec80 presence labels on the timeline evaluation videos; tune smoothing params on a subset.
steps: Run src.inference.detect_video (B's module, unchanged) on each timeline-eval video.
Implement src/timeline/evaluate.py: resample predictions to 1 fps; per-tool frame-level precision/recall/F1, and segment IoU; overall macro-F1.
Compare raw (no smoothing) vs smoothed; try 3–4 values of window_s and min_segment_s on the 1 tuning video, report on the 2 reporting videos.
Write docs/timeline/TIMELINE_EVAL.md with tables and one example timeline plot per video.
Update configs/timeline.yaml defaults to the chosen parameters.
accept: Per-tool F1 table for raw vs smoothed on held-out timeline videos.
Tuning and reporting videos are disjoint (stated).
Smoothed macro-F1 ≥ raw macro-F1.

resolutions.issue: Draft plan had 8 weeks / ~270 h of work; the real deadline is Wed 25 Nov 23:59 (≈2.5 days).
resolutions.fix: Re-planned into 7 dated work blocks with an MVP scope: 1 baseline + 2 tuning runs, 3 timeline-eval videos, a pilot usability test (≥3 people), a smoke checklist + 1 Playwright test, and a run script instead of Docker. About 25 h per member.

resolutions.issue: Inference module (B) originally waited on the first trained weights, which blocked the API (C) until Tuesday afternoon.
resolutions.fix: 3.3.1 is built Monday night against COCO-pretrained yolov8n.pt and swaps weights later; the dependency on 3.1.1 was removed.

resolutions.issue: Cholec80 access needs an approval request that will probably not arrive before the deadline.
resolutions.fix: 1.3.1 decides on Monday evening: use Cholec80 only if access already exists, otherwise use presence labels from held-out m2cai16-tool videos.

resolutions.issue: The web router and i18n loader (D) would have to import A's Analytics page and ar.json, so both would edit the same files.
resolutions.fix: D's shell auto-discovers pages and locale files with import.meta.glob. A adds files only inside their own paths.

resolutions.issue: A single requirements.txt would be edited by A, B and C at the same time.
resolutions.fix: Split into requirements/{base (D), data (A), ml (B), api (C)}.txt.

resolutions.issue: A's analytics charts may need a new npm package in web/package.json, which D owns.
resolutions.fix: A opens a PR that touches only package.json + lockfile; D approves it. Listed in shared-file rules.

resolutions.issue: Everyone writing one shared final report file would cause merge conflicts.
resolutions.fix: One file per section (01_data A, 02_model B, 03_system C, main + 00/04 D). D assembles them by include, not by copy-editing.

resolutions.issue: The benchmark (B) needs timeline F1 code that C owns.
resolutions.fix: B calls src/timeline/evaluate.py read-only. Signature changes go through C.

resolutions.issue: The API (C) needs PDF routing inside src/api/, which could collide with D's integration work.
resolutions.fix: C owns all of src/api/ including routes/reports.py. D owns only scripts/, docker/ and the root deployment files.

resolutions.issue: The slide deck originally depended on report sections that are finished in the last block, which left no time for slides.
resolutions.fix: 8.2.1 now depends on EDA, test evaluation and timeline evaluation (ready by Wed afternoon). Usability numbers are added in the final block.

resolutions.issue: Initial scaffold creates __init__.py stubs in every member's folder.
resolutions.fix: Scaffold exception: after the single scaffold commit by D, each path belongs only to its owner (CODEOWNERS enforces this).

gitFlow:
• main: protected, release only. D merges develop → main at the release candidate (Wed 20:00) and tags v1.0.0.
  • develop: protected integration branch. PRs only, 1 approval + green CI. D merges at merge windows: Mon 23:00, Tue 13:00, Tue 21:00, Wed 12:00, Wed 18:00.
  • Feature branches: one per WBS task, <member>/<wbs-id>-<slug>, e.g. c/4.1.1-smoothing. Branch from the latest develop and rebase before opening the PR.
  • PR rules: title [WBS 4.1.1] Temporal smoothing; touches only the owner's paths (CODEOWNERS auto-requests the right reviewer); includes tests and acceptance evidence; under ~400 changed lines where possible.
  • Contracts: any change to contracts/ is its own PR, approved by D and every consumer, and logged in contracts/CHANGELOG.md.
  • Conflicts: the integration owner (D) resolves merge conflicts on develop. Nobody edits another member's files to make their own PR pass; open an issue for the owner instead.
  • Never commit data/, frames, videos or *.pt weights. Share them via GitHub Release or the team drive.
